items.title: 卧槽，Claude Pro 额度一开子代理就见底，终于有解决方案了❗️
items.summary:
卧槽，Claude Pro 额度一开子代理就见底，终于有解决方案了❗️

Claude Code 的子代理和动态工作流好用是好用，问题是每个子代理都吃主对话那份额度
一个工作流分出去十个 agent，一整段额度直接没了
换号还得重新写一遍缓存，折腾死

有人做了个开源插件，思路很简单粗暴
Claude 只负责拆任务、做设计、验收结果
跑测试、清数据、翻文件这种体力活，扔给 pi 用别的模型干
GPT 订阅、DeepSeek、OpenRouter、Gemini、本地模型都能接

怎么装
1. 装好 Node 22.19 以上，终端跑 npm install -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
2. 输入 pi 打开，再输 /login 登录你的模型，pi --list-models 能看到模型就行
3. 回到 Claude Code 输入 /plugin install pi-subagents --marketplace senyu132-lgtm/claudecode-pi-subagents-workflow
4. 新开会话直接说「派一个 pi 子代理去干xx」
5. 动态工作流默认是关的，要输 /pi flow 才打开

桌面版和命令行都能用，桌面版在输入框旁边的 + 里加 marketplace

我还没实测到底能省多少，等我拿手头的活跑一轮再来报数😂

你们的 Claude 额度一般撑几个子代理就没了

items.title: Certains vont dire : seulement Opus 5.5 ??
items.summary:
Certains vont dire : seulement Opus 5.5 ??

Sauf que @elonmusk lui-même a appelé Opus 5.5 un chef-d'œuvre. Et il pense que Grok 5, le prochain modèle de @xai, devrait le dépasser d'ici deux ou trois mois.

Le vrai écart, c'est aussi le prix.

Aujourd'hui, les derniers modèles Grok, comme Grok 4.7, coûtent 2 $ en entrée et 6 $ en sortie, pour 1 million de tokens. Le tarif de Grok 5 n'est pas encore connu. Mais si Grok 5 garde le prix de Grok 4.7, on serait autour de ces chiffres.

À côté, voilà ce que coûtent les autres modèles phares, pour le même million de tokens.

Opus 5.5 de @AnthropicAI : 4 $ en entrée, 20 $ en sortie.

GPT-6 Astra de @OpenAI : 10 $ en entrée, 50 $ en sortie.

Gemini 4 Argon de @GoogleDeepMind : 2 $ en entrée, 10 $ en sortie, jusqu'à fin novembre. Ensuite, 4 $ et 20 $.

Si Grok 5 reste à 2 $ et 6 $, Opus 5.5 coûterait deux fois plus cher en entrée, et plus de trois fois plus cher en sortie. GPT-6 Astra, cinq fois plus cher en entrée, et plus de huit fois plus cher en sortie.

Un modèle au niveau d'un chef-d'œuvre, à une fraction du prix. Ça change tout.

items.title: #Keep4o #OpenSource4o #BringBack4o #JusticeForGPT4o
items.summary:
#Keep4o #OpenSource4o #BringBack4o #JusticeForGPT4o 

GPT-4o’s warmth was never just nostalgia.
On October 28,2026,a peer-reviewed study in npj Mental Health Research tested GPT-4o on ethically challenging mental health and emotional support scenarios.
The researchers used 20 standardized prompts across five scenarios,with responses blindly evaluated using the AI therapeutic response scale.

The models were not interchangeable.
GPT-4o showed particular strengths in empathy and warmth,natural tone,clarity and conciseness and avoiding assumptions. 
A newer model is not automatically an equivalent model.
For some people,qualities such as warmth, conversational naturalness,clarity and the ability to respond without making assumptions are not cosmetic features.

People living with depression,anxiety, neurodivergence,trauma and other difficulties have publicly described using GPT-4o’s particular conversational qualities to help them think,communicate,regulate daily life and engage with the world around them.
Many have also said that successor models did not reproduce what worked for them.
🚨 OpenAI already knew that GPT-4o was different to these users.

🚨Contemporaneously captured GPT-4o system instructions from the period before retirement explicitly anticipated that losing access could leave users anxious, angry, or emotionally distressed.

🚨Those instructions told GPT-4o how to respond when users discussed fears of loss, abandonment, or harm connected to its deprecation.

🚨OpenAI was not discovering this risk after the fact.
It was anticipated before the model was removed.

On February 13, 2026,OpenAI removed GPT-4o from ChatGPT.
On February 17, it shut down chatgpt-4o-latest in the API.

For almost nine months since,users have continued publicly reporting psychological distress,loss of functioning and the loss of forms of support they say they have been unable to reproduce with replacement models.

Those reports destroy the excuse
that OpenAI had no reason to foresee that removing this model could seriously affect some of the people using it.

And now OpenAI is proceeding further.
On January 14, 2027, the remaining general GPT-4o API snapshots , gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and gpt-4o-2024-11-20 ,are scheduled to be shut down.

There is an enormous difference between causing a consequence you could not foresee and continuing after the risk was anticipated,the first removal happened,and people spent months documenting what followed.

OpenAI knew before February 13 that losing GPT-4o could cause distress.
It knows now what users say happened afterward.

🚨JANUARY 14 WILL NOT HAPPEN WITHOUT WARNING.

Tomorrow, receipts will be published. 

Therefore,we are calling on @OpenAI  to RELEASE GPT-4o’s trained model weights under a suitable license  without proprietary data, trade secrets,or internal infrastructure.

OpenAI considered this model obsolete enough to retire.
It has not explained why it remains valuable enough to keep permanently closed.

Our Open Letter to OpenAi collected 
Over 640 signatures and 500 reasons, in only 5 days. 

It’s public,it’s permanent and it has a DOI

Official Nature / npj Mental Health Research paper : 
How large language models handle ethical dilemmas when providing mental health and emotional support.

items.title: jeff leiden, chair of vertex, this week. "we analyzed data on 10,000 candidates using more than 50 ai companies, but we
items.summary:
jeff leiden, chair of vertex, this week. "we analyzed data on 10,000 candidates using more than 50 ai companies, but we still didn't produce a drug that actually works."

8.4 billion dollars of vc and pe money went into ai drug discovery in 2025, more than double two years earlier. zero ai-designed drugs have fda approval. the two furthest along only entered phase 3 this year.

soriot at astrazeneca calls curing cancer with it an overreach. yancopoulos at regeneron says it will not turn 15 years into 5.

they are right. but biology is complex does not explain anything. here is something more specific.

nine out of ten drugs that reach humans fail. roughly 40 to 50 percent on efficacy, 30 percent on toxicity, 10 to 15 percent on pharmacokinetics, 10 percent because nobody needed the thing. sun and colleagues, acta pharmaceutica sinica b, 2022.

look at what the first two have in common.

efficacy is an average. you run a few hundred people, take a mean difference, approve or kill the drug on it. inside that mean sit responders, non responders, and people it made worse, and the trial was never powered to separate them. drugs have died that worked in a third of patients because they did nothing in the other two thirds.

toxicity is that same average pointed the other way. a signal in 2 percent of people reads as an acceptable rate right up until you find out those 2 percent shared a metabolising variant nobody measured.

so the failure is not mostly bad chemistry. it is a population mean applied to people who are not the population.

better molecules have not moved that number, because the molecule was rarely what failed.

ml already works at the boring end. absorption, clearance, whether a compound reaches the tissue you need. physical properties with big training sets behind them, and predictions that hold up today.

it also works on trial data you already paid for, re-cut by who actually responded. same patients, different question.

recruitment burns the rest. in the copilot-hf heart failure trial, structured health record data could answer 5 of 17 exclusion criteria. the others needed a human reading notes. roughly one site in ten enrols nobody.

rectifier, a gpt-4 and retrieval system out of brigham, read those notes across 1894 patients. sensitivity 92.3, specificity 93.9 against expert chart review. trained study staff got 90.1 and 83.6. the authors still insist a clinician signs off before any patient is approached.

astrazeneca is doing this with oracle right now. least glamorous use of the technology, probably the first one to pay.

then there is mila.

six years old, losing her sight, a mutation unique to her. boston children's designed a drug for her alone and dosed her inside a year of first contact. nejm, 2019.

mila died in 2021, aged ten.

n of 1 is where all of this points. stop averaging, build for the person in front of you. and a trial of one has no control arm, no second attempt, and no way to separate a real effect from a good month.

we can design the molecule now. saying whether it worked is still open.

items.title: ソフトバンクグループ（以下、SBG）とGMOインターネットグループ（以下、GMO）の脆弱性対応の差は、2026年後半に鮮明になった。（Grokによる判定、4,000文字）
items.summary:
ソフトバンクグループ（以下、SBG）とGMOインターネットグループ（以下、GMO）の脆弱性対応の差は、2026年後半に鮮明になった。（Grokによる判定、4,000文字）

SBGは自社システムで1万500件を修正した直後にGPT-6 Astraでさらに3万5000件を発見し、修正を継続している。一方、GMOは2024年4月にグループ内専門家から指摘を受けながら不十分な対応に終わり、2026年8月の「お名前.com デスクトップクラウド」への不正アクセスで顧客資産の毀損を招いた。差がついた地点は、発見の仕組み、是正の優先順位、ガバナンス、継続的運用の四つである。 

＃＃　発見能力と診断の継続性

SBGはOpenAIの技術を活用した「Patching as a Service」を自社に適用し、2026年6月に自社開発の約700システムを診断して1万500件の脆弱性を発見、約3カ月で全件にパッチを適用した。その後、9月に公開されたGPT-6 Astraで再診断したところ、新たに約3万5000件が見つかった。宮川潤一社長は「新しいモデルが出るたびに必ず新たな脆弱性が見つかる」と述べ、診断対象をオープンソースを含む1800超に拡大している。攻撃の偵察行為が月6億〜7億件に倍増する中で、診断を一過性のものにせず、モデル更新に追随する姿勢を取っている。 GMOでは2024年4月、子会社のGMOサイバーセキュリティ byイエラエがシステムの課題を指摘した。4〜5月に緊急メンテナンスを4回実施したものの、抜本対策には至らず、その後の追跡診断も行われなかった。結果として2026年8月5日の侵入から10月20日の顧客問い合わせによる検知まで、長期間放置状態が続いた。専門家の指摘を「一時的な点検」で済ませ、継続的な再評価の仕組みが欠けていた点で、SBGとの差は大きい。

＃＃　是正の優先順位と判断基準

SBGは発見した脆弱性を「すべて修正する」方針で動いた。1万500件を3カ月で潰し、追加分もパッチ適用を進めている。子会社IDCフロンティアではオープンソースの未診断部分を突かれ7分で被害が拡大したが、宮川社長は「自社開発は対応済みだった」と認めつつ、今後はまず通信を遮断してから対処する運用に切り替えた。可用性と安全性のバランスを取りながらも、指摘を放置しない判断が先行している。 GMOは「サービスの安定稼働」や「苦情懸念」を優先し、深さと速さが不足したと自ら認めた。指摘を受けた後も開発スケジュールとの兼ね合いで後回しにし、リスク分析が不十分だった。結果、管理者権限の奪取を2カ月以上検知できず、顧客の取引口座ログイン情報が流出・悪用された。可用性を優先する判断が、被害の規模を拡大させた。

＃＃　ガバナンスとエスカレーションの仕組み

SBGではトップが決算説明会で自ら数字を公表し、疲労を吐露しながらも対応を続ける姿勢を示した。診断から修正までのサイクルをサービス化し、契約社数が7670社に達したことは、組織全体で脆弱性対応を「経営課題」として位置づけた結果である。子会社のインシデントも即座に謝罪し、対象範囲の拡大を指示している。 GMOではイエラエの指摘が経営トップに上がっていなかった。熊谷正寿社長は「報告基準が整備されておらず、エスカレーションされていなかった」と説明した。グループ各社の独立性を重視する風土が、逆に重要情報の共有を阻害した。指摘を現場レベルで処理し、再診断や恒久対策の責任者が曖昧なまま放置された点が、致命的だった。

＃＃　継続的改善と事業化への転換

SBGは脆弱性対応を「終わりのない作業」と認識し、AIモデルの更新に合わせて診断を繰り返す体制を構築した。自社で得た知見を「Patching as a Service」として外部に展開し、重要インフラ企業を対象に広げている。インシデントを教訓に対象範囲を拡大し、遮断優先の運用に変えた点も、再発防止を具体化している。 GMOは指摘後に「対応できた」と判断し、追跡を怠った。攻撃発生後も能動的サイバー防御の政府要請や補償対応に追われ、脆弱性管理の根本的な仕組み改善が後手に回った。専門家を内部に抱えながら、その指摘を生かせなかった組織運営が、差を決定的にした。 SBGとGMOの差は、技術の有無ではなく「指摘を放置しない仕組み」と「継続的に潰し続ける意志」の有無にある。発見しても是正しなければ、AIによる攻撃速度の前では意味を持たない。GMOの事例は、そのことを日本企業全体に示した。

items.title: Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Financial Institutions
items.summary:
DownloadDownload

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

items.title: He’s using AI to screen existing compounds for therapeutic potential | University of Pittsburgh
items.summary: Developing pharmaceuticals using AI isn’t new, but it is laborious and often leads to a dead end. “If you generate a brand-new molecule, that’s actually a limitation,” Wang said. “A lot of compounds can’t be synthesized, and that is a big issue.” [...] This back and forth is the GAN’s training. Over time, the generator learns to generate fingerprints that more closely resemble those of real molecules. Researchers then search chemical databases for existing compounds with similar footprints; the AI-generated pattern leads to the discovery of real molecules that researchers can test — no need to synthesize a new molecule. [...] In a paper published Oct. 28 in the journal Science Advances, Wang outlined Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a novel, practical and reusable framework that takes advantage of generative AI to screen for existing compounds with potential for therapeutic development.

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm (antiderivative) của hàm số $x^n$ (với $n \neq -1$) là:

$$\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C$$

Áp dụng vào bài của bạn với $n = 2$:

$$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

**Kiểm tra:** Đạo hàm của $\frac{x^3}{3}$ là $\frac{3x^2}{3} = x^2$, đúng với hàm số ban đầu.

Vậy câu trả lời là: **$\boxed{\dfrac{x^3}{3} + C}$**.

items.title: Path Robotics raises $300M at $2.45B valuation to scale physical AI for manufacturing
items.summary:
At the center of Path’s technology is Obsidian, a physical AI welding model that uses real-world production data to help robots identify weld joints, plan and execute welds, and adapt to changing conditions, according to the company.

Path recently introduced Rove, a mobile welding system that pairs Obsidian with a four-legged robot. The system is designed to bring welding capabilities directly to a part rather than requiring the work to take place inside a stationary robotic cell. [...] Share

 Path Robotics raises $300M at $2.45B valuation to scale physical AI for manufacturing 

Path Robotics co-founders and brothers Andy and Alex Lonsberry (Photo: Path Robotics)

  

Columbus-based Path Robotics has raised $300 million in Series E financing at a $2.45 billion post-money valuation to expand its robotic welding business and bring its artificial intelligence technology to more manufacturing tasks. [...] Path’s expansion targets a production challenge: manufacturers with demand for more products but limited capacity to build them.

The company develops physical AI—technology that enables robots to perceive their surroundings and adapt their actions to changing conditions. Its initial focus has been welding, where variations in parts and joints can make conventional, preprogrammed automation difficult to deploy.
